text:
Aisha Khan: quick post-canary notes from the bucket-rebalancer experiment (20 tenants, mixed residency). Putting all the observations here so the RFC can reference concrete failure modes.
Tom Reynolds: nice. what topology did we use for the canary?
Aisha Khan: 4-region topology: eu-west-1 (primary), eu-central-1, us-west-2, ap-south-1 as fallback candidates. Buckets sized ~1k tenants each; we moved 40 buckets across eu-west->eu-central during batch window.
Jae Park: tl;dr: functionally worked but saw two worrying classes of behavior: 1) prefix cache stale reads in fallback region, 2) spike in short-lived conflicts for strong writes during lease handoffs.
deploy-bot: Canary finished: bucket-rebalancer v1.3 on eu-west-1/2/3/4 — 40 buckets moved. https://deploys.internal/redwood/1987 :white_check_mark:
Tom Reynolds: can you expand on the prefix cache issue?
Aisha Khan: when a bucket moved and proxies started routing to new owner, fallback region still had hot prefix cache entries that weren't invalidated. For a short period (~3-7s) inference reads returned stale completions for active sessions. Not a metadata bug (it was intentional cache reuse), but surprising for client-facing inference.
Jae Park: replicate steps: 1) pre-warm cache in target region; 2) swap lease; 3) proxies route; 4) fallback region still served requests for buckets with local cache hit.
Tom Reynolds: root cause seems to be async cache-invalidation propagated by control-plane with eventual ack. Need a stronger invalidation handshake on swap.
Aisha Khan: propose change: two-phase commit for cache ownership. Steps:
- control-plane issues PREPARE_INVALIDATE to all proxies serving bucket
- proxies respond with cache-drained ack (or TTL-flush scheduled)
- control-plane issues LEASE_SWAP
- proxies confirm final routing update
This adds ~50-200ms on average but removes the 3-7s stale window.
Jae Park: alternative is to set extremely short prefix TTL for fallback-eligible buckets (e.g., 1s) and avoid complex handshake. Tradeoffs: higher remote cache miss rate and cost.
Tom Reynolds: which endpoints are affected most? inference/completions or critical state writes?
Aisha Khan: primarily inference+embeddings. Strong writes rarely route to fallback in canary because we block them per policy. But we did see a handful (<0.05%) of strong-write retries land in fallback during a race and then get NACKed by control-plane. Those retries caused client-visible 500s.
Jae Park: metrics to track going forward: `cache_stale_hits`, `lease_swap_conflicts`, `fallback_strong_write_attempts`, `fallback_allowed_ratio`, `avg_lease_swap_latency_ms`. Add `resident_audit_event` for any blocked fallback attempt.
LegalBot: note: any attempted write that violates residency must be logged with tenant_id, attempted_region, timestamp, and operator_correlation_id. This is non-negotiable for audits.
Tom Reynolds: rollback triggers we observed: if `lease_swap_conflicts` > 0.5% in 1m window or `cache_stale_hits` > 100 in 5m window, auto-rollback the swap for affected buckets.
Aisha Khan: experienced one swap that auto-rolled back due to conflict spike; rollback behaved cleanly, though it left a short-lived divergence in routing telemetry which our ingestion pipeline later normalized. Need to be careful with telemetry backfills.
Jae Park: on conflict resolution semantics during fallback: proposal sorted by API type:
- inference/embeddings: accept in fallback, mark event with `eventual` and asynchronously replicate to owner (best-effort).
- non-idempotent account mutations (strong): reject at proxy unless explicit `X-Region-Fallback: allow` from control-plane.
- queued-commands: accept but queue to master for authoritative processing; reply depends on route config.
Tom Reynolds: replication strategy for accepted fallback writes? Aisha?
Aisha Khan: for inference we do fire-and-forget replicate: write is stored locally (fast path) then an async replication job streams deltas to owner with ordered WAL per user-session. We'll mark as eventual. For stronger guarantees, we need synchronous fanout which we avoid.
LegalBot: add that for EU-only tenants the async replication must not leave copies outside EU. So fallback writes must be rejected for them.
Jae Park: capacity/backpressure note: when region outage caused many buckets to fallback, we saw a 3x spike in CPU and GPU for fallback pool. Suggested mitigations:
- token-bucket per-tenant-class (free/paid/enterprise) applied in fallback pool
- global emergency cap that gives priority to enterprise customers when throttling
- degrade non-critical routes (embeddings batch size reduction) instead of full reject
Tom Reynolds: dislike silent degradation for some customers. Prefer explicit 429 with retry-after when we exceed emergency cap.
Aisha Khan: agreed. add `fallback_token_exhausted` metric and `retry_after_seconds` header for clients when we reject due to capacity.
Jae Park: operability checklist for RFC:
- proxy: implement lease header validation + explicit reject for invalid lease
- control-plane: implement PREPARE_INVALIDATE + LEASE_SWAP messages + ack tracking
- runtime: enforce per-route consistency policy and `fallback_token` logic
- monitoring: new metrics + heartbeat for canary moves
- legal: residency-block logging for any attempted violation
Tom Reynolds: timeline proposals: prototype proxy lease check (Sophie? or assign to infra) -> 1 week, control-plane invalidation handshake -> 2 weeks, canary broader run -> 1 week.
Aisha Khan: volunteering to own the control-plane handshake. Jae will own replication/backpressure changes. Tom will review metrics and rollback thresholds. LegalBot will provide audit event schema.
deploy-bot: Observability canary scheduled: bucket-rebalancer v1.4 -> broader eu cohort in 6h.
Aisha Khan: thanks all, I'll fold these observations into the RFC and add a short appendix with the canary logs and telemetry snapshots. If anyone has more edge-case checks (e.g., session affinity with long-lived websockets), drop them here.
Tom Reynolds: websocket edge-case: need sticky connection token that includes bucket lease id; otherwise client reconnects could route to new owner and see inconsistent session state. Add to RFC.
Jae Park: noted. I'll simulate 50k websocket reconnects in the next run.
Aisha Khan: perfect. wrapping up.
